title: Inkling eval scratchpad - Chiara
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to capture small-sample checks and an ad-hoc rubric while investigating the odd stability drop on model-v2-small (served via staging). Not a polished report — raw notes I can iterate on and hand off.

Quick summary:
- Observed: sudden uptick in low-coherence replies starting ~2024-10-15 (traffic routed to v2-small-canary).
- Magnitude: roughly 8-12% of a 200-sample smoke set showing truncated sentences / premature stop / repetition.
- Hypothesis: kernel selection path + new KV cache branch interacting with prefix caching; or prompt normalization change in request trimming layer.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick hand scoring, 0-4):
- Coherence (0: gibberish, 4: fully coherent and contextually correct)
- Instruction-following (0: ignores instruction, 4: exact/concise answers)
- Hallucination/Accuracy (0: contradicts facts, 4: correct or abstains when unsure)
- Verbosity/Conciseness (0: rambling, 4: right length)
- Latency/Token-bubble (0: obvious token loss / early stop, 4: normal)
Note: aim for 3+ as acceptable for targeted feature.

Sampling method:
- 100 examples: seeded prompts from customer-sim-queries.csv (mix of chat + single-turn instructions).
- 100 examples: random production-like prompts (anonymized) trimmed to 128 tokens.
- Run pairwise: baseline v2-small-2024-09-30 vs canary v2-small-2024-11-01 using identical seeds.

Representative samples (hand-annotated):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the key terms of this contract clause: ..."
   Baseline: "In short, the clause says the vendor is responsible for ..." (score: Coherence 4 / Instr 4 / Acc 4 / Verb 3 / Lat 4)
   Canary: "In short, the clause says the vendor is responsible for... In short, the clause says the vendor is responsible for... In short, the clause says the vendor is responsible for..." (score: Coherence 1 / Instr 2 / Acc 2 / Verb 0 / Lat 1)
   Notes: repeating loop, likely KV cache reuse gone wrong.

2) Prompt: "Write a short, friendly email declining a meeting and suggesting a later time."
   Baseline: Good 2-paragraph email (score Coherence 4)
   Canary: Short email but ends abruptly: "... please let me know a time that works for you." (stops mid-sentence sometimes) (score Coherence 2 / Lat 1)
   Notes: early termination signals increased.

3) Prompt: "Explain Newton's third law in one sentence for a 7th grader."
   Both models mostly fine; small variations. (scores baseline 4 / canary 3)

Quant signals observed (local run):
- Mean token count per reply: baseline 74, canary 59 (delta -20%)
- Repetition heuristic trigger (3x n-gram repeat): baseline 1.2% -> canary 7.8%
- Early-stop flag (abrupt end punctuation w/out sentence completion): baseline 0.9% -> canary 6.5%

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache indexing bug: duplicate pointers cause looped emission. Explains repetition.
2) Aggressive trimming in preprocessor: context trimmed incorrectly causing early stop.
3) New kernel branch for attention quantization changes termination condition.
4) Load-related behavior: canary pods under different batch scheduler config leading to partial state flush.

Quick repro steps I ran locally:
- reproduced on staging endpoint: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer test-key" -d '{"model":"v2-small-canary","prompt":"<seeded>" , "seed": 42}' https://staging.redwood/api/generate
- Logged raw token stream, compared to baseline stream.
- Instrumented KV cache metrics in logs (kv_hits, kv_size, kv_index). Saw occasional index collision warnings in one pod.

Notes to engineering (what I'd like from serving infra):
- Can we get a trace for one of the canary pod IDs that emitted the repeating sample? (I captured pod id: staging-pod-7f9c)
- Attach kernel selection trace around that request (want to see which path chosen).
- Increase sampling of stream logs for that shard for next 12 hours.

Quick triage conversation snippets (internal):
- Ethan: "saw kv index warning; will instrument additional asserts"
- Maya: "also patching trimming logic to log pre/post lengths"

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run the same 200-sample test with seed=999 and another seed to ensure not seed-specific.
- [ ] Run with prefix-caching disabled in config to isolate.
- [ ] Compare with v2-medium to check if problem scale-dependent.
- [ ] Add a metric in console: % replies flagged for repetition (daily) + cohort by model version.

Hypothesis experiments planned (short):
A) Toggle prefix-caching off (A/B) on a small traffic slice; compare repetition delta.
B) Force kernel selector to old path for one pod; re-run seeded suite.
C) Re-run with request-trimmer disabled and inspect pre/post prompt lengths.

Rough timeline:
- 10/18: noticed uptick, started smoke sampling.
- 10/19-10/22: pairwise sampling run + hand annotations (this doc).
- 10/23: Ethan to push assert/logs, Maya to add trimming logs.
- 10/24: plan to run A/B toggle for 6 hours and report.

Handy note: when scoring quickly, mark a sample as "repeat" if n-gram repeat >2 AND contains exact phrase repeated at least 2x. Saves time.

Scratch hypotheses for root cause mapping to code areas (notes to self):
- kv index collision -> serving-runtime/cache/kv_index.*
- trimming weirdness -> platform-ingress/prompt_trim.py (new change in PR #629)
- kernel termination mismatch -> serving-runtime/kernels/torch_attention.cpp (recent micro-optimizations)
- batch scheduler flush -> platform-routing/batch_manager.go

If I hand this off: immediate asks:
- Label a few failing samples as priority and attach the full token stream + pod trace (Maya/Ethan).
- Add a short dashboard tile: "repetition rate by model" for quicker ops eyes.

Random personal notes (brain-dump):
- Might be worth a small fuzzer that inserts repeated prefix tokens and ensures no unbounded repetition.
- Add a short test in CI that runs a 50-seed micro-suite post any cache or kernel change.

End of scratchpad. Will refine into a mini-POSTMORTEM once we have traces.

-- chiara
